diseases.name: Fall armyworm, Spodoptera frugiperda
symptoms: Scrapping of leaf surface by young larvae.
Older larvae, feeds upon central whorl, causing extensive defoliation.
Whorl, tassel and cob fed by larva.
Egg masses (120-150 eggs/ egg mass) covered with scales
Larvae wit h 4 black spots arranged (in square shape) on 8th and 9th abdominal segment
Larvae with inverted shaped mark on head
Male adult moth forewing brown with triangular white spots; femalesâ forewing  grayish brown.

management_practices: Apply neem cake @ 250 kg/ha at the time of last ploughing.
Seed treatment with cyantraniliprole 19.8% + thiamethoxam 19.8% FS @ 4 ml/kg seed.
Border cropping with cowpea, gingelly, redgram or sunflower (garden land) and fodder sorghum (dry land) @ 3 rows.
Set up FAW pheromone traps @ 12 nos./ha
Spray azadirachtin 1500 ppm @ 2.5 lit/ha or chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 200ml/ha (or) flubendiamide 480SC@ 250ml/ha at early stage (15 - 20 DAE).
Spray Metarhizium anisopliae (TNAU-MA-GDU isolate) @ 2.5 kg/ha or emamectin benzoate 5 SG @ 200g/ha or novaluron 10 EC @ 750 ml/ha or spinetoram 11.7 SC @ 250 ml/ha at late whorl stage (35 - 40 DAE).
One of the insecticides recommended in late whorl stages can be used at cob formation stage if needed, but repetition to be avoided.

diseases.name: Shoot fly: Atherigona orientalis
symptoms: Infests crop from 2 days to 3 weeks after emergence.
Maggots feed on young growing shoots causing  dead heart
Eggs white, elongated, looks like a rice grain.
Yellowish maggots.
Pupa dark brown, barrel-shaped.
Adult, small grey coloured

management_practices: Seed treatment with imidacloprid 70 WS 10 g/kg or imidacloprid 600 FS @ 6 ml/kg or thiamethoxam 70 WS @ 3.5 ml/kg.
Remove and destroy stubbles
Spray methyl demeton 25EC 1000 ml/ha or dimethoate 30EC 1155 ml/ha
Set up fish meal trap @ 12 nos./ha till up to one month.

diseases.name: Stem borer: Chilo partellus
symptoms: Central shoot dries leading to dead heart
Young larva feeds tender folded leaves causing âshot holeâ symptom.
Old larvae bores stem and feeds on internal tissues.
Bore holes and tunneling noticed on stem.
Yellowish brown larva with brown head
Straw coloured moths

management_practices: Inter-crop maize with cowpea in 2:1 ratio.
Release egg parasitoid, Trichogramma chilonis @ 2,50,000 /ha thrice at weekly intervals.
When infestation crosses 10%, spray dimethoate 30EC  660 ml/ha or chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @150 ml/ha

diseases.name: Pink stem borer: Sesamia inferens
symptoms: Pink larva damage stem leading to dead heart
Bead like eggs laid in rows within leaf sheath
Pinkish brown larvae with dark head
Straw coloured moths with white wings

management_practices: When infestation crosses 10%, spray phosalone 35EC 1150 ml/ha or chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @150ml/ha twice at 20 days interval

diseases.name: Corn worm / Earworm: Helicoverpa armigera
symptoms: Larva feeds on silk, developing grains and cobs.
Spherical, creamy white eggs.
Greenish to brown larva with brown lines dorsally white lines laterally
Brown pupa on soil, leaf or crop debris
Light pale brownish moth. Forewings olive green with brown circular spot in the centre
Hind wings smoky white, with broad black outer margin.

management_practices: Set up of light traps @ 1 no./ha.
Set up Helicoverpa sex pheromone traps at 12 nos./ha
Two applications of NPV at 10 days interval at 1.5 X1012 POB along with Crude sugar 2.5 kg + cotton seed kernel powder 250 g on the ear heads.
Spray malathion 5D 25 kg/ha or phosalone 4D 5 kg/ha
Updated on May 2023

diseases.name: Ear head bug: Calocoris angustatus
symptoms: Nymphs and adults are seen on earhead and sucks juice from grains at milky stage.
Grains shrink and turn black becomes ill filled or chaffy
Blue cigar shaped eggs, laid under glumes or middle of the florets.
Slender green coloured nymphs
Adults: male greenish; Female green with brown margin

management_practices: Apply malathion 5D 25 kg/ha or phosalone 4D 25 kg/ha or neem seed kernel extract 5% or Azadirachtin 1%  @ 1 lit/ha on 3rd and 18th day after panicle emergence

diseases.name: Web worm: Cryptoblabes gnidiella
symptoms: Larva first feeds on the lemma of the flowers scraping the chlorphyll, later on the milky grains.
Webbing of maize cobs and feeding on the flowers and the grains
Larva: Long and dark brown
Adult: Dark grey forewings
Pupa : Pupal period 10-12 days.

management_practices: Apply neem seed kernel extract 5% or azadirachtin 1% @ 1 lit/ha on 3rd and 18th day after panicle emergence.

diseases.name: Ash weevil: Myllocerus sp.
symptoms: Grubs feed on the secondary rootlets
Adults cause irregular notching on the leaf margins
Adult: Grey coloured weevil
Larva: Grubs have four instars. Larval period -  55 â 70 days.
Pupa: Pupation occurs in soil. Pupal period 23 - 33 days.

management_practices: Apply Neem cake @ 500 kg/ha at the time of last ploughing.

diseases.name: Leafhopper: Pyrilla perpusilla
symptoms: Leaves become yellow
Covered with black sooty mould
Top leaves get dried up and lateral buds germinate
Nymph: Soft, pale brown dorsally and pale orange ventrally
Adult: Straw coloured, head pointing forward as a snout

management_practices: Avoid excessive use of nitrogenous fertilizers
Detrash at 150 th and 210 th DAP
Release lepidopteran parasitoid: Epiricrania melanoleuca @8000-10,000 cocoon/ha (or) 8-10 lakhs egg/ha
Spray malathion 50EC 2000 ml/ha

diseases.name: Aphid or Plant lice:Â Rhopalosiphum maidis
symptoms: Yellowing of leaves
Colonies of aphids found in leaf whorl and cob sheath.
Yellowish with dark green legs

management_practices: Seed treatment with thiamethoxam 70%WS @ 3.5 g/kg seed
Conservation of natural enemies such as coccinellids, chrysopids and syrphids

diseases.name: Shoot bug: Peregrinus maidis
symptoms: Plants become unhealthy stunted and yellow
The leaves wither from top downwards
Panicle formation is inhibited and the plants die if attack is severe.
Honeydew secreted by the bug causes growth of sooty mould on leaves.
Midribs turn red due to egg-laying and may dry up subsequently.
Egg : Laid inside the leaf tissue and covered with a white waxy substance
Adult : Yellowish brown to dark brown with translucent wings

management_practices: Spray dimethoate 50 EC @ 1000 ml/ha
